After that, you run for 5km and measure the time.
If you can do it in less than 25 minutes, you are good.
If not, you need to train and check until you have achieved this goal.
After that, you can get your starting number.
Depending on when your work day ends, you have to find out whether you can go there from home, or need to leave directly from work.
If more than one hour is left between your starting time and the end of your workday, you can go there from home.
Else, you need to leave directly from work.
While running at the Night Run, you run and drink at the same time.
In the end, you receive your final running time.

Some of the above information you have to enter into the app, some of the information is collected by fitness gadgets.

Give it one outgoing branch for the continuing activity and one for the newly started activity, both unconditional. Do not place an exclusive gateway or a decision condition on these concurrent branches, and do not sequence the continuing activity after the new one.

When the description names several activities that must all be finished before the process moves on or ends, and it gives no order among them: Model a parallel gateway that splits into those activities as concurrent branches, and a second parallel gateway that joins the branches before the next element or the end event. Do not chain the activities in a fixed sequence, and do not join them with an exclusive gateway.

When the description states that one activity is always performed, while a second activity that runs alongside it is performed only if a stated condition holds, and both paths must rejoin before a later step: Model an inclusive gateway as the split. Give the always-performed activity an unconditional outgoing flow, and give the conditional activity an outgoing flow labeled with the condition. Close both paths with a matching inclusive gateway before the later step. Do not use a parallel gateway for the join, because it would wait for the skipped branch, and do not use an exclusive gateway, because it would not synchronize the always-performed branch with the conditional one.

When the description states that one actor performs two activities at the same time (simultaneously, with no order between them), so both activities run concurrently and are not a single combined step: Model each of the two simultaneous activities as its own task. Open them with a parallel gateway and close them with a parallel gateway before the next step, so the step continues only after both branches have run. Do not merge the two activities into one task, and do not place a decision on the branches.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.

result.rule: When the description states an activity as a verb and object, followed by a purpose, scope or qualifying clause in the same sentence: Name the task with the verb and object of the stated activity, using the description's own words, and leave the purpose or scope clause out of the task label. Do not append words from that clause, and do not add a qualifier the description does not attach to the activity itself.

When the description attributes an action to the system itself (for example, the system shows information or checks a condition) rather than to a human participant: Model that action as a service task placed in the lane or pool of the system, labelled with the system as subject plus the verb and object the description states. Do not model it as a manual task or as a user task carried out by the human actor, and do not drop the system from the label.

When The description states that an activity is carried out with or obtained from a specific party or source (for example, a task that gets items from a named group of people, or contacts a named party), so the source is part of the stated action.: Label the task with the verb the description uses for the action and name the party or source it involves, so the label keeps the stated source and does not generalize to a broader or different action such as receiving or handling items without saying where they come from.

When the description states that a participant carries out an activity that takes time and is not an external occurrence being awaited (no message, signal, timer or condition is awaited), even if the description phrases the end of the process around that activity: Model that participant activity as a task labeled with the verb and main object the description uses for it. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event, because a catch event represents the occurrence of an external event, not work the participant performs.
